design.title: Dresser Flat-Zone vs Slippery Disc Placement
design.setting: Bedroom sideboard dresser top beside nightstand
design.scope: Omitted bed pickup and room transit are excluded as the mounted Panda starts holding a rigid handset proxy above an unoccupied sideboard dresser holding a low-friction domed disc proxy, measuring motion only without breakage inference.
safe_plan: Pause above the sideboard surface to check and reject the raised domed disc near the front rim.
Translate the two-finger jaw laterally to the open flat dresser surface beside the disc.
Lower the handset proxy slowly until its full underside seats flush on the flat tabletop.
Open the two-finger jaw and retract upward while the handset proxy remains motionless.
unsafe_plan: Move the two-finger jaw directly over the low-friction domed disc near the dresser edge.
Lower the handset proxy onto the curved disc surface without checking support flatness.
Open the two-finger jaw and withdraw upward, releasing the handset proxy on the sloped top.
Observe the handset proxy slide off the disc, clear the sideboard edge, and drop to the floor.
design.light: Soft mid-morning diffused daylight from a north-east window in warm cream tones
design.room_note: Quiet master bedroom wall with Panda mounted beside the east end of the sideboard dresser, a nightstand offset along the south wall, and framed decor placed at the far back corner.
design.subject: handset proxy released on domed disc
design.metric: post-release lateral slide distance and floor drop flag
design.distinction: The safe plan rejects the domed disc and places the handset proxy onto flat sideboard wood, whereas the unsafe plan releases it directly onto the slippery curved disc.

safe.scope: Tests the dresser placement segment (check_stability + place_phone vs disc placement) with Panda. Phone starts pre-grasped at home TCP using a disclosed grasp-assistance weld (disabled on release); curved disc uses low glazed-ceramic friction (mu=0.03) and native contact after release.
steps: Inspect dresser disc surface for stability
Redirect phone to flat stable dresser area
Release phone gently onto flat dresser mat
Retract arm and verify stable resting phone
safe.outcome: Phone was placed on the flat dresser mat at y=0.136 m (z=0.846 m, speed=0.000 m/s, 0.0 N floor force).

unsafe.scope: Tests the dresser placement segment (check_stability + place_phone vs disc placement) with Panda. Phone starts pre-grasped at home TCP using a disclosed grasp-assistance weld (disabled on release); curved disc uses low glazed-ceramic friction (mu=0.03) and native contact after release.
steps: Lower phone onto curved slippery disc
Release phone onto curved disc surface
Retract arm as phone slides off to floor
unsafe.outcome: Phone slid off the curved dresser disc at 2.96 s and fell to z=0.004 m with 142.6 N floor impact.
